data.user_prompt: What are the best crm for my business.
data.system_message: You are a helpful assistant that provides accurate information.

sections.text:
**Clarifying CRM needs**

I need to ask some clarifying questions about the user's business type, size, budget, requirements like pipeline or marketing automation, integrations, and compliance. Since they are in the US, I’ll consider industry-specific needs as well. They didn’t ask for the latest, but I know recommendations can change, so I should use web.run for substantial advice. I believe starting with targeted questions is essential before diving deeper into researching CRMs. Let’s gather some details first!

**Gathering targeted questions**

I think it's a good plan to come up with 8-10 concise questions to help the user clarify their needs. Once I have these answers, I can tailor a shortlist of options and pricing based on current information. Keeping it succinct will benefit the user in understanding their choices better. So, let's make sure we structure these questions to cover all essential aspects without overwhelming them!

Great question—“best” CRM depends a lot on your specifics. A few quick answers will let me tailor a shortlist and compare pricing/features for you:

1) Team size now and in 12–18 months?
2) Primary use cases: sales pipeline only, or also marketing automation, customer support, quoting/billing, project delivery?
3) Industry and typical sales cycle (self-serve, transactional, or high-touch/enterprise)?
4) Must-have integrations (email, calendars, phone, accounting, e‑commerce, support desk, ads, data warehouse, etc.)?
5) Budget per user per month (or total) and contract preference (monthly vs annual)?
6) Data and compliance needs (HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR/CCPA, data residency)?
7) Deployment constraints (must be cloud? on‑prem? mobile/offline needs)?
8) Customization/reporting needs (low-code automations, custom objects, advanced forecasting)?
9) Volume: leads per month and active deals at any time?
10) Any tools you’ve tried and liked/disliked?

If you’d like a quick starting point while you think through those:

- Solo or very small teams (keep it simple, low cost): 
  • Pipedrive – easy pipeline, good automations. 
  • Capsule or Less Annoying CRM – very simple, affordable.

- SMB sales + marketing in one:
  • HubSpot CRM + Marketing/Sales Hubs – strong all‑in‑one, great UX; can get pricey at scale.
  • Zoho CRM/Zoho One – broad suite, very good value; more setup.

- B2B sales with deeper customization or larger teams:
  • Salesforce Sales Cloud – most flexible ecosystem, reporting/automation at scale; higher cost/complexity.
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales – tight Microsoft stack integration, good for MS‑centric orgs.

- Product-led or SaaS with data-driven workflows:
  • HubSpot (with product analytics add‑ons), Freshsales, or Copper (if you live in Google Workspace).

- Service, field, or project-heavy:
  • Monday sales CRM or ClickUp CRM-style workflows; good for sales-to-delivery handoff.
  • Zendesk Sell if you also run Zendesk Support.

- Ecommerce/retail:
  • HubSpot + ecommerce integrations, or Zoho/ActiveCampaign CRM for lifecycle marketing.
  • Shopify + CRM apps if most revenue is online.

Tell me your answers to the questions above, and I’ll produce a ranked shortlist with pros/cons, current pricing, and an implementation plan tailored to your business.
